text:
marie: quick question — noticed 2–3% tail spikes on L4 when we end up switching kernels mid-request. are SM capability checks done per-request or per-session? :thinking:
jon: per-session today. the capability probe runs at allocation/attach time. if we hit an unsupported op during execution we currently take the slow fallback in-place.
sasha: can you paste the unreliable log lines? curious which kernel throws the fallback.
marie: here's the snippet:
```
2026-03-18T14:22:11Z AttnKernel: dispatch fused_attention_wmma failed -> unsupported_wmma, falling back
2026-03-18T14:22:11Z Runtime: switching to attention_scalar (memcpy path)
```
marie: model is a 7b-family, head_dim=128, seq_len=4096, batch=1. spikes correlate with longer sequences.
kevin: L4 lacks the full WMMA set so fused kernels get disabled. runtime falls back to slower matmul+memcpy path which explains the tail.
kevin: tradeoff: we do cheap per-session probing to avoid expensive per-request checks, but that means a session pinned to a kernel that later becomes suboptimal as seq lengths vary.
sylvie: proposal: introduce a small "kernel_fitness" signal computed at allocation time. score = function(hw_caps, model_meta, expected_seq_dist). store in request/session meta and use it for routing + cache key. avoids mid-run surprises. :bulb:
jon: sounds reasonable. concerns: computing fitness adds CPU work to cold starts and affects cache locality because cache keys change. also complexity in rollout/metrics.
marie: alternate thought — microprobe the real-attention path by running a single short forward (e.g., first token) with candidate kernels to measure latency/peak-sm occupancy. that picks the fastest kernel for the real model shape. runtime already has a probe harness but it's heavy.
kevin: microprobe is nice but on L4 the probe itself might trigger the same fallback and still be costly. maybe combine heuristics: quick static score + optional microprobe for long-seq/high-cost models.
sasha: also need to consider multi-tenant Dedicated nodes: you can't run probes that disrupt other customers. microprobe should be opt-in per-ppool or limited by budget.
jon: implementation sketch: add kernel_fitness (int) to AllocationMetadata, populated by ProbeManager. Router uses fitness to prefer routes and to choose fallback thresholds. If runtime detects mid-exec fallback, emit a signal to increment a degradation counter for that allocation.
sylvie: and an auto-escalation rule: if degradation_counter > 3 within N mins, mark allocation as "unstable" and trigger reallocation with different kernel hints.
marie: example check code for capability fallback detection:
```
sm_caps = runtime.query_sm_cap()
if not (sm_caps & HAS_WMMA):
  kernel_hint = "scalar_attn"
else:
  kernel_hint = "fused_wmma"
```
kevin: plus an extra heuristic: if seq_len > 2048 and head_dim <= 128, prefer matmul-optimized kernel regardless of WMMA. empirically it beats fused for L4 shapes.
jon: open questions: where do we store fitness in the cache key? it affects hit rates. do we version it? and how to surface metrics in Console?
sasha: metrics: per-allocation fallback count, kernel_latency_p95 per kernel variant, kernel_switch_events. then we can build a regression alert if a new model or kernel increases fallback rate.
marie: action items: I will open an RFC issue with design + perf microbench plan. kevin, can you prototype kernel_fitness calcs (static heuristics) and a short sim? jon, can you add `allocation.degradation_counter` metric to the runtime? sylvie, can you outline the canary policy for automatic reallocation? infra-bot: canary-rollout scheduled for next week if RFC lands. :white_check_mark:
jon: agreed. tagging this as follow-up for runtime-kernel-selection epic.
marie: thanks all — will drop the RFC link here when created. :pray:
